title: Gratin de Courgettes
subtitle: A Provencal courgette gratin with eggs and Gruyere
excerpt: Sliced courgettes baked with egg, cream, and Gruyere until golden and set. Light enough for summer but satisfying as a main with bread and salad.
sourceNotes: Provencal summer gratin. Courgette water is the main risk; salting first solves it.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Salt and drain the courgettes up to 2 hours ahead. Assemble and bake just before eating.

content.text: Courgettes hold a lot of water. Salt them first, squeeze them dry, and the gratin will set firm instead of going soggy. The egg and cream custard holds everything together.
Toss the courgette slices with the salt in a colander. Leave for 20 minutes, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can with your hands.
Heat the oven to 190C. Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and courgettes to the pan. Cook for 5 minutes, turning often, until lightly coloured.
Beat the eggs with the cream, half the cheese, the thyme leaves, and some pepper.
Tip the courgette mixture into the gratin dish. Pour the egg mixture over. Scatter the remaining cheese on top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until set in the centre and golden on top. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The gratin is watery after baking.
items.cause: The courgettes were not drained or squeezed well enough.
items.fix: Squeeze as firmly as possible and cook off any remaining moisture in the pan before assembling.

items.symptom: The centre is still liquid after the bake time.
items.cause: The egg mixture needed more time to set.
items.fix: Bake for a further 10 minutes. The gratin is done when it no longer wobbles in the centre.

items.cause: The oven was not hot enough or the dish was too deep.
items.fix: Switch to the grill for the last 3 minutes to colour the surface.
